title: Build point-charge slab model
action: Construct a 7×7×4 array of point charges (±1 e) at NaCl lattice sites with the NaCl lattice constant d+− = 2.814 Å, representing the (100) surface. This array will be used as the external electrostatic field in all subsequent SCF calculations.

title: Isolated CO2 SCF reference calculation
action: Perform a single-point SCF calculation on an isolated CO2 molecule (C–O bond length 1.162 Å, linear) using the STO-6G basis set to obtain the reference total energy E_isolated, needed for Δ_SCF.

title: Compute adsorption energies for all models
action: Using the point-charge substrate and the isolated CO2 reference energy, compute the total adsorption energy Δ = Δ_SCF + Δ_DR. The electrostatic/polarization contribution Δ_SCF is obtained from SCF calculations of CO2 in the external field. The dispersion-repulsion term Δ_DR is evaluated with a London pair potential whose coefficients are derived from ionization energies, polarizabilities, and van der Waals radii. For the hard-sphere model A1: compute Δ for perpendicular adsorption above a Na+ ion (site 1) at distance z = 2.35 Å, and for parallel adsorption above a Na+–Na+ alignment with C at the center of a Na2Cl2 square (site 2) at z = 2.336 Å. For the softened model A2: for the parallel orientation at site 2, for each λ in {1.1, 1.2, 1.26, 1.3}, minimize the total energy with respect to the molecule–surface distance z to obtain equilibrium distance z_m and Δ. For the cluster model B: treat the (CO2Cl2)2‑ cluster in the remaining point-charge field, minimize z, and compute Δ. Output all computed adsorption energies and distances to adsorption_energies.csv.
description: CSV file containing adsorption energies and equilibrium distances for all models and configurations.
output_schema: Columns: Model (string, one of A1, A2, B), Orientation (string, 'perpendicular' or 'parallel'), Site (string, surface site label), Lambda (float or empty, softening parameter), z_equilibrium (float, Angstrom), AdsorptionEnergy (float, kcal/mol). Required rows: A1 perpendicular site1, A1 parallel site2, A2 for λ=1.1,1.2,1.26,1.3, B.

title: Compute ν2 vibrational frequency shifts
action: Using the equilibrium geometries from the previous step, determine the potential energy surface along the ν2 bending coordinate of CO2 for each model (A1, A2, B). For model A₂, use the equilibrium geometry obtained with λ = 1.26 (the softening parameter that gives the same molecule–surface distance as the hard-sphere model). Compute harmonic force constants, account for anharmonicity, and derive the vibrational frequencies for the in-plane (ν_parallel) and out-of-plane (ν_perp) bending modes. Report the shifts ν_perp − ν2, ν_parallel − ν2, and ν_perp − ν_parallel. Output the results to vibrational_shifts.csv.
description: CSV file with vibrational frequency shifts for the ν2 bending mode.
output_schema: Columns: Model (string, A1, A2, B), nu_perp_minus_nu2 (float, cm-1), nu_parallel_minus_nu2 (float, cm-1), nu_perp_minus_nu_parallel (float, cm-1).
